summary: Narrow read-only profiling on the original local PDFs, using test-only scripts in /tmp. No DB, network or app changes. ROOT CAUSE: fz_run_display_list takes 85% (Jan) to 99% (Apr) of cold validation time. MuPDF decodes and downscales the page images again for every clip. A DisplayList stores only the drawing operations, not the decoded images, so reusing it saves almost nothing (building the lists took only 9ms and 5ms in total). Prototype: render one whole-page pixmap per page at 0.3, then cut each crop out with integer slicing. This is 3.5x faster on Jan (4736 -> 1360ms) and 26x faster on Apr (9200 -> 357ms), and uses less memory. However, the slices are NOT pixel-identical to the clip renders, and the differences are inside the crops, not only at the edges. The validation output is thrown away, so a whole-page render can still serve as the decodability check, as long as every per-ref geometry and omit check stays in place.

Jan24S1.page_pt: 2479x3508, scanned, up to 27 images per page
Jan24S1.pixel_match: 0 of 201 identical; all 201 differ inside the crop (max abs diff up to 182); shapes and origins match

Apr08S2.pixel_match: 0 of 199 identical; 7 differ only at the edge, 192 differ inside the crop (sampled max abs diff 54-78)

diagnostics.interpretation: Apr pages are small, but every 0.3 clip makes MuPDF decode the full-resolution embedded image again (~47ms per clip), and nothing is reused between clips. The differences inside the crops most likely come from image resampling and anti-aliasing changing with the clip origin. Whole-page slicing must therefore NOT replace the full-resolution delivery renders; use it only for the low-res validation, whose output is discarded.

wholepage_validation_equivalence: Still needed, unchanged: the sha256 check, the page-range check, the rect non-empty and inside page.rect check, and the omit_rects-inside-crop check. These are pure geometry and must run for EVERY ref, including an invalid last one; the prototype ran page.rect.contains before rendering. Decodability: a full-page render draws everything on the page, including every image that any ref touches. That makes it stricter: it could fail on a corrupt image that no ref uses. MuPDF also often only warns on decode errors, in both paths. Not verified with a corrupted-image fixture yet; a test is needed.

encoding_12_fullres_crops_scale2.note: The mupdf CPU figure includes the render; the others are encode-only. Recommendation: if payload size matters, switch to Pillow PNG compress_level=6. It keeps the PNG format, is ~19% smaller on scans and costs modest CPU. Do not use optimize=True. WebP would need Accept negotiation plus a PNG fallback; not implemented.

useAttempt_route_switch_race.status: UNREPRODUCED. No browser or React test was run within the time budget. This is a code-review risk only, NOT a verified bug.
useAttempt_route_switch_race.evidence: The /attempts/:id route renders the same <Player/> element, so navigating from A to B reuses the same hook instance. load() (useAttempt.js:69-100) has no id or staleness guard. A late response for A runs data.current=d and setAttempt(d), so A's data would show in B's view. Also, loading.current is still true from A, so B's load returns early.
useAttempt_route_switch_race.minimal_fix: In App.js, key Player by user.id+id, for example a small wrapper that uses useParams and renders <Player key={`${user.id}:${id}`}/>. A's hook instance then unmounts on navigation. Optionally, also guard setState after await with a requestId or mounted ref so late callbacks are dropped.

next_minimal_implementation: In validate_source_crops only: render ONE full-page pixmap per page at 0.3 (alpha=False, keep at most 1-2 cached). Keep every per-ref geometry and omit check. Skip the PNG encode and gray check because the output is unused. Expected cold time: ~1.4s (Jan) and ~0.36s (Apr).
Keep the delivery _render_crop_png (scale 2) on the clip path, because whole-page slices are not pixel-identical.
Gray conversion was useful for 0 of 400 crops; it costs only ~20ms, so removing it is optional.
Add a test with a corrupted embedded image on a ref page to confirm both paths reject it the same way.
